;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019–2021 Iraqi protests]]
**Gunmen in vehicles open fire on protesters in [[Baghdad]], killing over 19 and injuring around 70 others. Three of the dead were [[Iraqi Police|Iraqi police]]. The victims were either stabbed or shot. [https://apnews.com/2d15fae86ea3e86dcf417f1d26a3461b (AP)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2019/12/06/gunmen-cars-kill-least-15-injure-scores-baghdad-protests/ (''Telegraph'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/middleeast/2019/12/killed-central-baghdad-assailants-fire-live-rounds-191206190824237.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019 Kenya bus shooting]]
**At least ten people – including seven [[Kenya Police|police officers]] – are killed when gunmen ambush a bus in Kotulo, [[Kenya]]. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claimed responsibility for the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kenya-attack/at-least-eight-killed-in-kenya-in-suspected-islamist-militant-attack-idUSKBN1YA27Z (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/10-killed-kenya-bus-attack-claimed-al-shabab-191207082718077.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Naval Air Station Pensacola shooting]]
**A shooter kills three people and injures eight more at [[Naval Air Station Pensacola]], [[Florida]], [[United States]], before being shot and killed by police. [https://www.pnj.com/story/news/2019/12/06/breaking-active-shooter-reported-base-nas-pensacola/4351773002/ (''Pensacola News Journal'')]
**The shooter was a [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] national who was being trained at the Naval station. His name was later released to be Mohammed Saeed Alshamrani. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/12/06/us/pensacola-naval-station-lockdown/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Islamists kill 17 civilians in two attacks in eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security/islamist-rebels-kill-at-least-17-in-eastern-congo-local-official-idUSKBN1YA1YJ (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A collision between a [[U.S. Navy]] boat and a [[U.S. Coast Guard]] boat in [[Kodiak, Alaska]]'s [[Womens Bay, Alaska|Womens Bay]] injures nine, one critically. [https://www.stripes.com/news/coast-guard/coast-guard-navy-boats-collide-in-alaska-nine-injured-1.610036 (''Stars & Stripes'')]
*A gas explosion and consecutive fire in an apartment building in [[Prešov]], Slovakia killed at least seven people and injured dozens. [https://www.dw.com/en/slovakia-7-die-in-gas-explosion-dozens-injured/a-51559162 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2019/12/07/world/europe/ap-eu-slovakia-gas-explosion.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 Samoa measles outbreak]]
**Samoan police arrest Edwin Tamasese, an [[Anti-vaccine activism|anti-vaccination]] campaigner, for incitement against a [[Government of Samoa|government]] order. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-12-06/anti-vaxxer-charged-samoa-amid-nationwide-immunisation-drive/11772714 (ABC Australia)]
*The [[United States District Court for the Central District of California]] rejects a [[U.S. dollar|US$]]190 million [[defamation|defamation suit]] against entrepreneur [[Elon Musk]] by [[Tham Luang cave rescue]]r Vernon Unsworth. The lawsuit, considered to be the first major suit by a private individual over comments made on [[Twitter]], was filed over Musk's insulting Tweets after Unsworth criticized his role in the rescue. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-musk-lawsuit/tesla-boss-elon-musk-wins-defamation-trial-over-his-pedo-guy-tweet-idUSKBN1YA13U (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Dominican general election]]
**People in [[Dominica]] head to the polls to elect the members of the [[House of Assembly of Dominica]]. The governing [[Dominica Labour Party]] gathers the most votes and stays in power for another legislation. [https://dominicanewsonline.com/news/homepage/homepage-carousel/breaking-news-dlp-wins-again-according-to-unofficial-reports/ (Dominica News Online)]
